Case: Entire page including marketing panel re-renders in the selected language when the language picker is used
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the login or signup page at sso.sleekflow.io. Language picker is visible.
  • Source: [sleekflow-login-signup-011 · AC1]
  • Traceability: "Language picker with 9 languages; the whole page, marketing panel included, re-renders; Arabic is right-to-left. (UX-01)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the login page at sso.sleekflow.io.
  2. Locate the language picker.
  3. Select a different language (e.g., Bahasa Indonesia).
  4. Observe the entire page including the marketing panel on the left/right.
Expected:
• All page text (form labels, buttons, links) is rendered in the selected language.
  • The marketing panel content is also translated to the selected language.
  • No English text remains visible (except brand names like "SleekFlow").
BDD: Given a user is on the auth page, When they select a language from the language picker, Then the entire page including the marketing panel re-renders in the selected language

Case: Arabic layout switches to right-to-left when Arabic is selected from the language picker
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the login or signup page. Language picker is visible.
  • Source: [sleekflow-login-signup-011 · AC1]
  • Traceability: "Arabic is right-to-left."
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the login page.
  2. Select Arabic from the language picker.
  3. Inspect the page direction (dir attribute on html/body or computed style).
  4. Observe the visual layout of form fields, labels, and marketing panel.
Expected:
• The page direction is set to RTL (dir="rtl" on html or body element).
  • Form fields and labels are right-aligned.
  • Marketing panel layout is mirrored to RTL orientation.
  • No layout overflow or broken alignment is visible.
BDD: Given a user selects Arabic from the language picker, When the page re-renders, Then the layout switches to right-to-left with correctly mirrored elements

Case: Every input field on the login page has a visible label and associated error element
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the login page at sso.sleekflow.io.
  • Source: [sleekflow-login-signup-011 · AC5]
  • Traceability: "Every input has a label and an error element; a live region announces errors; password toggle is a labelled switch. (UX-05)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the login identifier page.
  2. Inspect each input field for an associated visible label (label[for] or aria-label).
  3. Trigger validation errors on each field.
  4. Verify each field has an associated error element.
Expected:
• Every input field has a programmatically associated label (via label[for] or aria-label/aria-labelledby).
  • Each field has an associated error element that becomes visible on validation failure.
BDD: Given a user is on the login page, When they inspect the form fields, Then every input has a label and an associated error element

Case: Error messages are announced by a live region when form validation fails
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the login or signup page.
  • Source: [sleekflow-login-signup-011 · AC5]
  • Traceability: "a live region announces errors"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the login page.
  2. Submit the form with empty fields to trigger validation errors.
  3. Inspect the DOM for a live region element (aria-live="assertive" or "polite").
  4. Verify the live region content updates with the error text.
Expected:
• A live region element (aria-live) exists on the page.
  • When a validation error occurs, the live region content is updated with the error message text.
BDD: Given a user triggers form validation errors, When errors appear on the page, Then a live region announces the error messages for assistive technology

Case: Password visibility toggle is implemented as a labelled switch accessible to assistive technology
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the login password step or signup password step where a password toggle is visible.
  • Source: [sleekflow-login-signup-011 · AC5]
  • Traceability: "password toggle is a labelled switch"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the login flow and proceed to the password step.
  2. Locate the password visibility toggle (eye icon or similar).
  3. Inspect the toggle for ARIA role and label.
  4. Click the toggle and verify it changes password field visibility.
Expected:
• The password toggle has a descriptive ARIA label (e.g., "Show password" / "Hide password").
  • The toggle has an appropriate role (button or switch).
  • Clicking the toggle changes the password field type between "password" and "text".
BDD: Given a user is on the password step, When they interact with the password visibility toggle, Then it is accessible with a descriptive label and toggles visibility correctly

Case: PostHog anonymous ID is captured on sign-up completion
Description:
• Pre-condition: User completes the full signup flow. PostHog analytics is active on the page.
  • Source: [sleekflow-login-signup-011 · AC6]
  • Traceability: "PostHog anonymous ID on sign-up. (UX-07)"
Test Steps:
1. Open browser developer tools Network tab.
  2. Complete the full signup flow (email, terms, password, submit).
  3. Observe network requests for PostHog calls.
  4. Inspect the PostHog request payload for an anonymous ID.
Expected:
• A PostHog network request is captured during or after signup completion.
  • The request payload includes an anonymous_id or distinct_id field.
BDD: Given a user completes the signup flow, When the signup succeeds, Then a PostHog event with an anonymous ID is captured
